claims.text: refund-design.md@stage-2 lines 3-5: status 'đề xuất, chưa làm'; the team reviews it like a pull request before writing code; it answers refund-requirements.md YC-1 to YC-10; risks are tracked in risk-register-example.md.

Lines 7-12 (summary): the API only records the request in the database and answers at once; a background job sends it to the gateway, retries with backoff and sends the same idempotency key each time; main reason: YC-7.

Step 1: POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/refund checks ownership and paid status, writes a pending refund row in the existing payments table with who and when, returns 202 Accepted, and does not call the gateway.

Steps 3-6 (planned, not built at stage-2): a job built like NotificationSender sends due rows with key refund-<row id> (YC-9); retries after 1, 2, 4, 8 min, at most 1 h apart, for 24 h (YC-10); on confirmation the order becomes cancelled and an email is queued (YC-5).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-2: docs/design/refund-design.md:25-37; no refund code in DonHang.Api/Domain/Infrastructure

claims.text: Lines 39-43: the rejected option, calling the gateway in the customer's request, is simpler (no status column, no job) but on gateway failure or slowness the customer waits and gets an error and the request is not recorded; it contradicts YC-7.

Not in the design: no new table, no separate payment service, no gateway calling back; risks: R2 (no idempotency keys: step 4 becomes a status query before each resend), R1 (results only by callback: step 6 changes; known after the test-environment week).

Open question in the design: PATCH /api/v1/orders/{id}/cancel still cancels a paid order today (Order.Cancel() blocks only cancelled and shipped), though the app has no cancel button; the product owner decides whether to block it.
Lines 65-70: a history with version 1 at Sprint 15 planning; when the plan changes, the file is edited in the same pull request as the code, so it does not describe only the first idea.

A design doc written before building lets others find problems while changing the plan costs an edit; it should name rejected options with the requirement that ruled them out, be short, be reviewed like a PR and be updated with the code; anyone building the feature can write one.

Step 2 adds columns to payments (kind, status, requested_by, requested_at, attempts, next_attempt_at, failure_reason); the PATCH cancel open question exists so that every paid order goes through the refund flow.

self_check.notes: Quotes refund-design.md@stage-2 1-12 and 39-43. No decision records or team-wide comment process, no architecture diagram, no code. R1 tech: steps described as planned ('would'); Đơn Hàng's same-PR rule conditioned; 'can stay short'. R1 junior: big upfront design and agile glossed; product owner role dropped; steps numbered; R1/R2 described; why PATCH cancel matters; backoff wording; q1 a, q4 d, q6 b reworded.
